translation_notes: prefixes: DC->dc, DCTERMS->dcterms, DOAP->doap, OWL->owl, PROV->prov, RDF->rdf, RDFS->rdfs, SDO->sdo, SKOS->skos

Two reads kept as two nested m{ }, NOT fused into one multi-pattern join: the outer loop body writes METADATA["uri"] between the two reads (a join would repeat it per (p, o) row), and the third read (objects of o for doap:repository) is fed by o only inside ONE branch (p == prov:wasGeneratedBy) -- a join would silently drop every row without a repository. Reads are therefore not a true conjunctive chain (cf. ldpy/016).
@graph self.G designates the graph of the stand-in self once, so the three m{ } are receiver-less; the original spelled self.G three times.

Context: self (a pyLODE VocPub) is a driver-local stand-in (FakeVocPub) with only G, METADATA, COLLECTIONS, CONCEPTS, outputformat, _make_formatted_uri and _make_agent; the two helpers are reconstructions (pyLODE 2.13.2 is not installable). `markdown` is the real installed package. original.py untouched.

Driver: 6 calls (full fixture html/md, two schemes, non-http source/licence + literal/URI-without-repository wasGeneratedBy, ValueError on missing title, zero schemes with a preset title); fixture holds a skos:Concept, owl:Ontology, skos:Collection and a foreign prov:wasGeneratedBy that must not be read. Verified by mutation: replacing doap:repository or skos:ConceptScheme in the translation makes check FAIL.
An m{ } with a literal bound in subject position ({o} = Literal) yields no solution rather than raising, like G.objects(subject=Literal).
optimization_notes: optimized.py (the same rewrite as the sibling OntDoc._extract_metadata region): the seven branches that store `str(o)` under a fixed key (title from skos:prefLabel, versionInfo, the three dates, the two vann properties) become one `text_keys` dict and one `if p in text_keys` branch; definition and historyNote share one branch, as do source and license (same http test, key = the dcterms local name); the agent branch stores its conditional expression directly; the three `set()` initialisations become one `METADATA.update(...)`; `len(X.keys()) > 0` becomes `if X:` on the two dicts. The predicates are pairwise distinct, so at most one branch fires per triple: read order, the ValueError guard and the last-wins repository are unchanged.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: the three reads become `m{ ?s a skos:ConceptScheme }`, `m{ {s} ?p ?o }` and `m{ {o} doap:repository ?o2 }` under `@graph self.G`; namespace terms become prefixed names (dict keys included) and the two vann URIRef(...) become IRIs. The notation ratio is held back by the header's nine @prefix lines (three unused), see the header variant.
No exception to the symmetry. The reads are not fused: uri is written per scheme between them, and the doap:repository read happens in only one branch.
header_optimization_notes: Python: BNode, DC and RDFS go; the rdflib import is sorted (Literal, URIRef).
LD Python: URIRef, BNode and the whole rdflib.namespace import go (the prefixes replace them); @prefix dc:, rdf: and rdfs: go (rdf:type is written `a`); markdown and Literal stay.
